correctness.rationale: An exact definition-based exhaustive certificate visits every canonical ternary word of length at most eleven and all nonempty position-subsets, aggregating occurrence coverage masks for every distinct subsequence. A candidate covers iff its union mask is complete; minimizing length therefore lists every shortest s-cover. Restricted-growth representatives enumerate all alphabet-renaming orbits bijectively. The program visits 72,517,166 nonempty occurrence subsets and confirms the sole ambiguous canonical length-eleven word, its two length-six covers, and six relabelings. A separate full labeled-word algorithm based on greedy extreme embeddings finds the same result, testing all \(3^{11}=177{,}147\) length-eleven words and shorter hosts. Explicit two-occurrence witnesses cover all 11 positions for each claimed cover. All bounds and computations are genuinely exhaustive for the stated finite domain; no inference beyond eleven is asserted.

originality.rationale: The primary 2022 conference paper (Section 5) introduces an alphabet-four, length-fifteen nonunique shortest s-cover example and a ternary pair of unequally long covers; the expanded 2025 paper (Section 7) retains the four-letter example. Neither inspected result gives the length-eleven sharp ternary threshold, the one canonical exceptional word, or its exact two-cover classification. Algorithms for a shortest cover do not by themselves imply exact enumerative ambiguity counts. Targeted literature searches and published research-index searches found no equivalence, but literature-index incompleteness remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: A previously published enumeration in a sequence database, unindexed thesis, or independent source may present the same complete finite classification.
Search exhaustiveness is not priority proof; the full-text comparisons establish only that the specifically inspected published versions do not directly subsume the claim.
The finite code is reproducible but has not been subjected to an external independent mathematical audit.

value.rationale: Multiplicity of minimum-length scattered-subsequence covers is a natural structural departure from classical string covering, where the shortest cover is unique. The known constructive example of two shortest covers uses four symbols and fifteen positions. A complete sharp ternary threshold and single six-word symmetry orbit at length eleven characterize the first possible ambiguity on the smaller alphabet, with concrete paired cover witnesses. This is a motivated exact boundary and finite classification, not a routine value of an arbitrary parameter or a mere relabeling of a prior example.
